body.translated_text: The <s>Paramārtha Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Ultimate Chanting of Names) of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Jñānasattva</s> (Wisdom-Being)
Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> in the form of a youth

children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>,
the supreme tamer of the untamed,
the hero victorious over the three worlds,
the king of secrets, lord of the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt),
with eyes like fully opened lotuses,
with a face like a blossoming lotus,
brandishing the supreme <s>vajra</s>
in his own hand again and again,
together with <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>-Taraṅga and other chief
innumerable <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>s (vajra-holders),
heroic tamers of the untamed,
bearing heroic and terrifying forms,
brandishing with their own hands
blazing points of <s>vajra</s>s,
through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
supreme benefactors of the world,
with delighted, satisfied, and joyful minds,
bearing forms of wrathful bodies,
performers of the deeds of a <s>Buddha</s>, protectors,
together with those whose bodies are bowed in reverence,
having bowed to the protector, the perfectly awakened one,
the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One),
having joined his palms together,
standing before him, spoke thus:
For my benefit, for my sake,
out of compassion for me, O all-pervading one,
so that I may attain the awakening
of the <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion),
for the sake of all beings
sunk in the mire of ignorance, whose minds are afflicted by <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements),
for the benefit of all sentient beings,
for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit,
may the perfectly awakened one,
the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Teacher, the Guru of the world,
the knower of the truth of the great <s>samaya</s> (sacred bond),
the supreme knower of the faculties and dispositions of beings, reveal it!
Of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>jñānakāya</s> (wisdom-body),
of the great <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance), the Lord of Speech,
of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Jñānasattva</s> (wisdom-being),
the embodiment of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), the self-arisen one —
the <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names) of profound meaning, of noble meaning,
of great meaning, incomparable, auspicious,
beneficent in its beginning, middle, and end,
the supreme <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>,
which has been spoken by past <s>Buddha</s>s,
which will be spoken by future ones,
and which the perfectly awakened ones of the present
speak again and again,
which in the great <s>tantra</s> of the <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion)
is sung
by the great <s>Vajradhara</s>s with delight,
by immeasurable holders of <s>mantra</s>s —
I too shall hold this
with firm resolve until final <s>niryāṇa</s> (passing),
so that I may become, O Protector,
the keeper of the secrets of all <s>Saṃbuddha</s>s (Fully Awakened Ones).
I shall proclaim it to beings
according to their various dispositions,
for the destruction of all <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements) without remainder,
for the elimination of all ignorance without remainder.
Having thus requested, the lord of secrets,
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, before the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
having joined his palms together,
stood before him with body bowed.

body.translated_text: Sixteen verses of supplication.

children.translated_text: Then <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
the perfectly awakened one, supreme among bipeds,
extending his long and broad
beautiful tongue from his own mouth,
displaying a smile that
purifies the three lower realms of existence for all worlds,
illuminates the three worlds,
and is the teaching that conquers the four <s>Māra</s>s (demonic forces),
with a <s>Brāhmī</s> (divine) voice, sweet,
filling the three worlds,
he addressed the lord of secrets,
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength:
"Excellent, O glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>!
Excellent, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>!
You who, for the benefit of the world,
are endowed with great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
are prepared to hear from me
the <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> of great meaning, pure, destroyer of sin,
of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s <s>jñānakāya</s> (wisdom-body),
from me.
Very well then, I shall teach this,
O lord of the <s>Guhyaka</s>s (secret ones).
Listen with one-pointed mind!"
"Very well, O <s>Bhagavān</s>," he replied.

body.translated_text: Six verses of response.

children.translated_text: Then <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
surveying the great <s>mantrakula</s> (mantra-family) with all its parts,
the family of <s>mantra</s> and <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder),
the three families:
the worldly and supramundane family,
the great <s>Lokāloka</s> (world and non-world) family,
the supreme family of the <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (Great Seal),
the great family of the <s>Mahōṣṇīṣa</s> (Great Crown),

body.translated_text: Two verses on surveying the six families.

children.translated_text: He spoke this verse
conjoined with the arising of non-duality,
having the nature of non-arising,
as the six <s>mantrarāja</s>s (mantra-kings), of the Lord of Speech:

children.text: a ā i ī u ū e ai
children.translated_text: a ā i ī u ū e ai

children.text: o au aṃ aḥ sthito hṛdi
children.translated_text: o au aṃ aḥ — established in the heart.
I am the embodiment of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), a <s>Buddha</s>,
of all <s>Buddha</s>s abiding in the three times.
Oṃ! Homage to you, O <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s> (Sharp Vajra), embodiment of the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) that cuts through <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering),
Lord of the <s>jñānakāya</s> (wisdom-body) and of speech, <s>Arapacana</s>!

body.translated_text: Three verses on the stages of <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion) awakening.

children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>Buddha</s>,
a <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One), born from the syllable 'A',
the syllable 'A' is the foremost of all phonemes,
of great meaning, the supreme imperishable syllable.
The great vital breath, truly unborn,
free from verbal utterance,
the foremost cause of all speech,
the supreme radiance of all words.
Great festivity, great <s>rāga</s> (passion)!
He who brings delight to all beings.
Great festivity, great <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion)!
The great enemy of all <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements).
Great festivity, great <s>moha</s> (delusion)!
The destroyer of delusion in the deluded-minded.
Great festivity, great <s>krodha</s> (wrath)!
The great and mighty enemy of great wrath.
Great festivity, great <s>lobha</s> (greed)!
The destroyer of all greed.
Great desire, great bliss,
great joy, great delight!
Great form, great body,
great color, great appearance,
great name, great generosity,
having a great and vast <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle).
Bearer of the great weapon of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the foremost goad-hook against the great <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements),
of great fame, of great renown,
of great radiance, of great splendor.
The wise bearer of great <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
the accomplisher of the purpose of great <s>māyā</s>,
delighting in the play of great <s>māyā</s>,
the great magician of <s>Māyā</s>'s net.
The supreme lord of great <s>dāna</s> (generosity),
the foremost upholder of great <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline),
the steadfast upholder of great <s>kṣānti</s> (patience),
of great <s>vīrya</s> (energy) and valor.
Abiding in the great <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),
bearing the body of great <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
of great strength, of great <s>upāya</s> (skillful means),
an ocean of <s>praṇidhi</s> (aspiration) and <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom).
Pervaded by great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), immeasurable,
of great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), of supreme intellect,
of great <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), of great intelligence,
of great <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), of great accomplishment.
Endowed with the power of great <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power),
of great speed, of great swiftness,
of great magical power, called the Great Lord,
of great strength and valor.
The smasher of the great mountain of <s>bhava</s> (existence),
the mighty bearer of the great <s>vajra</s>,
greatly fierce, greatly terrible,
inspiring fear in the face of great terror.
The supreme lord of great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge),
the guru of the supreme great <s>mantra</s>,
mounted upon the path of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle),
supreme in the method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.translated_text: Fourteen verses on the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> (Vajra Realm).

children.translated_text: <s>Mahāvairocana</s> (Great Illuminator), a <s>Buddha</s>,
the great silent sage, the great <s>Muni</s> (Sage),
arisen from the method of the great <s>mantra</s>,
whose nature is the method of the great <s>mantra</s>.
Having attained the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections),
the support of the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s,
the purity of the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s,
the method of the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s.
The lord of the ten <s>bhūmi</s>s (stages), the protector,
established on the ten <s>bhūmi</s>s,
whose nature is purified through the ten <s>jñāna</s>s (knowledges),
the upholder of the purity of the ten <s>jñāna</s>s.
Having ten aspects, whose purpose is the ten meanings,
the lord of <s>Muni</s>s (sages), possessing the ten powers, the all-pervading one,
the accomplisher of all universal purposes without exception,
the great one who masters the ten aspects.
Without beginning, whose nature is free from elaboration,
of pure nature, whose essence is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
a speaker of truth, one who speaks as things are,
one who acts accordingly, whose speech is not otherwise.
Non-dual, and a speaker of non-duality,
established at the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>),
the lion's roar of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness),
terrifying to the deer-like <s>tīrthika</s>s (heretical teachers).
Going everywhere, of unfailing course,
swift as the mind of a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), conqueror of enemies, victorious,
a <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Monarch) of great power.
Chief of the assembly, teacher of the assembly,
lord of the assembly, master of the assembly, sovereign,
of great majesty, the foremost,
not led by others, of great method.
Lord of speech, master of words, eloquent,
<s>Vācaspati</s> (Lord of Speech), of infinite utterance,
truthful in speech, a speaker of truth,
the teacher of the four <s>satya</s>s (Noble Truths).
Truly irreversible, a non-returner,
a solitary rhinoceros, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> leader,
gone forth through various modes of liberation,
the sole cause of the great elements.
An <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), with outflows exhausted, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant),
free from <s>rāga</s> (passion), with senses conquered,
having attained security, having attained fearlessness,
cooled, truly free from turbidity.
Endowed with knowledge and conduct,
<s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone), supreme knower of the world,
free from possessiveness, free from ego,
established in the method of the two <s>satya</s>s (truths).
Standing at the further shore of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),
one who has done what was to be done, standing on firm ground,
consumed by the fire of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute) knowledge,
wielding <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as a weapon, the cleaver.
The true <s>Dharma</s>, the King of <s>Dharma</s>, radiant,
the supreme illuminator of the world,
the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the Sovereign of <s>Dharma</s>,
the teacher of the path to the highest good.
<s>Siddhārtha</s> (One Whose Aim is Accomplished), of accomplished resolve,
free from all conceptual intentions,
free from conceptual construction, the imperishable element,
the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality), supreme, immutable.
Possessing merit, an accumulation of merit,
wisdom itself, the great mine of wisdom,
possessing wisdom, knower of being and non-being,
endowed with the two accumulations.
Eternal, universal sovereign, a <s>yogī</s>,
<s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) itself, the object of meditation, lord of intellects,
to be known through direct personal experience, truly immovable,
the supreme primal one, bearer of the <s>Trikāya</s> (Three Bodies).
A <s>Buddha</s> whose nature is the five <s>kāya</s>s (bodies),
the all-pervading one whose nature is the five <s>jñāna</s>s (wisdoms),
crowned with the five <s>Buddha</s>s as his diadem,
possessing the five eyes, bearer of non-attachment.
The father of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the son of the <s>Buddha</s>s, supreme and excellent,
born from <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>bhava</s> (existence), without a womb,
whose source is <s>Dharma</s>, the ender of <s>bhava</s> (existence).
Whose essence is compact and solid like a <s>vajra</s>,
newly born, lord of the world,
arisen from the sky, self-arisen,
the great fire of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).
<s>Vairocana</s> (The Illuminator), of great radiance,
the light of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), the shining one,
the lamp of the world, the torch of <s>jñāna</s>,
of great brilliance, luminous.
The king of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), lord of the foremost <s>mantra</s>s,
the king of <s>mantra</s>s, accomplisher of great purposes,
the great <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> (Crown), the wondrous <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s>,
the all-seeing one, lord of the sky.
The foremost embodiment of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the eye of joy for the world,
of universal form, the creator,
and the venerable, the honored one, the great <s>Ṛṣi</s> (Seer).
The bearer of the three families, the <s>mantra</s>-adept,
upholder of the <s>mantra</s> of the great <s>samaya</s> (sacred bond),
the supreme bearer of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels),
the supreme teacher of the three <s>yāna</s>s (vehicles).
<s>Amoghapāśa</s> (Infallible Noose), victorious,
<s>Vajrapāśa</s> (Vajra Noose), the great seizer,
<s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> (Vajra Hook), the great lasso,
inspiring terror like <s>Vajrabhairava</s>.

body.translated_text: Twenty-five verses minus a quarter on the wisdom of the completely pure <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality).

children.translated_text: The wrathful king, six-faced, terrifying,
six-eyed, six-armed, mighty,
with fearsome fangs and skeletal form,
with a hundred faces dripping deadly poison.
<s>Yamāntaka</s> (Destroyer of Death), king of obstacle-removers,
<s>Vajravega</s> (Vajra Speed), the terrifying one,
<s>Vighuṣṭavajra</s> (Resounding Vajra), <s>vajra</s> of the heart,
<s>Māyāvajra</s> (Illusion Vajra), great-bellied one.
Lord of the <s>vajra</s>, born from the <s>vajra</s>,
<s>Vajramaṇḍa</s> (Vajra Essence), like space,
the immovable one with a single mass of matted hair,
wearing a moist elephant hide.
Making the sound 'hāhā,' greatly terrifying,
making the sound 'hīhī,' frightful,
with a burst of laughter, a great laugh,
a <s>vajra</s> laugh, a great roar.
<s>Vajrasattva</s> (Vajra Being), great being,
<s>Vajrarāja</s> (Vajra King), great bliss,
<s>Vajracaṇḍa</s> (Fierce Vajra), great joy,
<s>Vajrahūṃkāra</s>, maker of the Hūṃ sound.
Bearer of the <s>vajra</s> arrow as weapon,
<s>Vajrakhaḍga</s> (Vajra Sword), the cutter,
bearer of the <s>viśvavajra</s> (double vajra), the <s>vajra</s>-holder,
the single <s>vajra</s>-holder, victorious in battle.
With eyes blazing with <s>vajra</s> flames,
with hair of <s>vajra</s> flames,
possessed by <s>vajra</s>, of great possession,
hundred-eyed, with <s>vajra</s> eyes.
With a body of sprouting <s>vajra</s> hairs,
having a form entirely of <s>vajra</s> hairs,
with nails sharp as millions of <s>vajra</s> points,
with skin compact and hard as <s>vajra</s> essence.
The glorious wearer of a <s>vajra</s> garland,
adorned with <s>vajra</s> ornaments,
resounding with the sound of 'hāhā' and bursts of laughter,
the <s>vajra</s> voice, of six syllables.
<s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Sweet Voice), of great sound,
the great and supreme hero of the three worlds,
extending to the limits of the realm of space,
the voice, the best among the voiced.

body.translated_text: Ten and a half verses minus a quarter on <s>Ādarśajñāna</s> (Mirror-like Wisdom).

children.translated_text: The selflessness that is the reality of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), beyond syllables,
the bull among proclaimers of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
with a deep and noble roar.
The <s>Dharma</s>-conch of great sound,
the <s>Dharma</s>-gong of great resonance,
of non-abiding <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
the <s>Dharma</s>-drum of the ten directions.
Formless, yet supreme in possessing form,
of manifold forms, mind-made,
the splendor that manifests all forms,
bearing all reflections without exception.
Invincible, called the Great Lord,
the Great Lord of the three realms,
established on the exalted <s>Āryamārga</s> (Noble Path),
<s>Dharmaketu</s> (Banner of Dharma), of great arising.
With the body of the sole youth of the three worlds,
yet an elder, an ancient one, lord of creatures,
bearing the thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (marks of a great being),
beautiful, the most handsome in the three worlds.
The teacher of worldly knowledge and virtues,
the teacher of the world, confident,
protector, savior, trusted by the three worlds,
refuge, guardian, unsurpassed.
Whose enjoyment is the expanse of the sky,
an ocean of omniscient wisdom,
the smasher of the egg-shell of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
the destroyer of the cage of <s>bhava</s> (existence).
One who has pacified all <s>saṃkleśa</s>s (afflictions) without remainder,
one who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),
crowned with the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom),
adorned as a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One).
The pacifier of the three sufferings of <s>duḥkha</s>,
having three ends, infinite, attaining the three liberations,
freed from all obscurations,
having attained the equality of space.
Having transcended the stain of all <s>kleśa</s>s (defilements),
having gone beyond the path and non-path of the three times,
the great <s>nāga</s> (serpent-lord) among all beings,
the crest-jewel of those bearing the crest of virtues.
Completely free from all <s>upadhi</s> (substrates of existence),
well-established on the path of space,
bearer of the great <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem),
the all-pervading one, supreme among all jewels.
The great flourishing <s>Kalpataru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree),
the supreme great <s>Bhadraghaṭa</s> (auspicious vessel),
the doer and maker of the welfare of all beings,
the well-wisher, tender toward beings.
Knower of the auspicious and inauspicious, knower of time,
knower of <s>samaya</s> (sacred bonds), keeper of <s>samaya</s>, all-pervading,
knower of the faculties of beings, knower of the right moment,
skilled in the three types of liberation.
Virtuous, knower of virtues, knower of <s>Dharma</s>,
renowned, the arising of auspiciousness,
the most auspicious of all auspicious things,
fame, fortune, glory, and goodness.
A great festival, a great comfort,
great bliss, great delight,
honor, reverence, prosperity,
joy, splendor, lord of glory.
The most worthy, the best bestower of boons,
worthy of refuge, the supreme refuge,
the supreme enemy of great fear,
the destroyer of all fears without remainder.
Crested, wearing a peacock crest, with matted locks,
wearing matted hair, shaven-headed, wearing a crown,
five-faced, with five crests of hair,
bearing a diadem of five hair-braids.
Upholder of the great vow, wearing the <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja grass girdle),
a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), supreme in vows,
of great <s>tapas</s> (austerity), devoted to austerity,
a ritual bather, of the <s>Gautama</s> lineage, foremost.
Knower of <s>Brahman</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> himself,
one who has attained <s>Brahmanirvāṇa</s> (liberation in Brahman),
release, liberation, a limb of <s>vimokṣa</s> (emancipation),
deliverance, peace, auspiciousness.
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> (cessation), bliss, tranquility,
the highest good, final departure, the ender,
the one who ends both pleasure and pain, the final goal,
<s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), the exhaustion of the substrates of existence.
Unconquerable, incomparable, unmanifest,
without appearance, without stain,
without parts, all-pervading, pervasive,
subtle, the seed, without outflows.
Dustless, free from dust, immaculate,
with faults expelled, free from affliction,
fully awakened, of awakened nature,
omniscient, all-knowing, supreme.
Gone beyond the nature of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) and <s>dharma</s>s,
<s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), bearing the form of non-duality,
free from conceptual construction, without elaboration,
accomplishing the deeds of the <s>Buddha</s>s of the three times.
Without beginning or end, a <s>Buddha</s>,
the <s>Ādibuddha</s> (Primordial Buddha), without lineage,
whose sole eye is <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), stainless,
the embodiment of <s>jñāna</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
Lord of speech, the great debater,
king of debaters, bull among debaters,
the best and most excellent among speakers,
the lion of debate, undefeated.
The all-seeing one, the joyful one,
the garland of radiance, the beautiful one.
The auspicious mark, the luminous one, the brilliant one,
the light, the one whose hands radiate splendor.
The supreme great physician, the best,
the remover of thorns, the unsurpassed one.
The tree of all medicines,
the great enemy of the disease of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).
The ornamental mark of the three worlds, the lovely one,
the glorious one, the circle of stars.
Extending to the sky in the ten directions,
with the great elevation of the banner of <s>Dharma</s>.
The one vast canopy over the world,
the circle of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion).
The glorious lord of the lotus dance,
with a jewel parasol, the great lord.
The great king of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the holder of the self-nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The great <s>yoga</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the one teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The glory of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel consecration,
the supreme lord over all jewels.
The master of all <s>Lokeśvaras</s> (world-lords),
the sovereign of all <s>Vajradharas</s>.
The great mind of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the mental course of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The great body of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The <s>vajra</s>-sun, the great light,
with the stainless radiance of the <s>vajra</s>-lord.
The great passion beginning with dispassion,
with brilliance blazing in all colors.
Seated in the <s>vajra</s>-posture of perfect awakening,
the holder of the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>'s chanting.
The glorious one, born from the <s>Buddha</s>-lotus,
the holder of the treasury of omniscient wisdom.
The king who bears universal illusion,
the great holder of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.
The <s>vajra</s>-sharp one, the great sword,
the pure one, the supreme imperishable syllable.
The great vehicle that cuts suffering,
wielding the great weapon of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>.
The conqueror of conquerors, of <s>vajra</s>-profundity,
of <s>vajra</s>-intelligence, the knower of truth as it is.
The fulfiller of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
the ornament of all <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).
The pure selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>,
with the moonlight of perfect wisdom in his heart.
The great endeavor of the net of illusion,
the supreme lord of all <s>tantras</s>.
With inexhaustible <s>vajra</s>-seat,
the holder of the complete wisdom-body.
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Sumati</s>,
<s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, the sustainer of the world.
The great womb of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the holder of the wheel of universal creation.
Supreme in the self-nature of all existences,
the holder of the self-nature of all existences.
Of unborn nature, serving the purpose of all,
the holder of the self-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.
The greatly wise one in a single instant,
the holder of the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>.
The realization of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the sage of ultimate reality, of foremost intellect.
Calm, with a thoroughly serene self,
the holder of the awakening of a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>.
Directly perceived by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the flame of wisdom, the greatly luminous one.

body.translated_text: Forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment.

children.translated_text: The supreme accomplisher of desired goals,
the purifier of all evil destinies.
The highest of all beings, the protector,
the liberator of all beings.
The sole hero in the battle against <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the destroyer of the pride of the enemy of ignorance.
Wisdom personified, bearing the erotic sentiment, glorious,
bearing the forms of the heroic and the horrific.
Swinging hundreds of arm-staffs,
dancing with foot-stamps.
The glorious one with the expanse of a hundred arms,
dancing in the expanse of the sky.
Having trod upon the surface of the earth with one foot-sole,
standing on the circle of the great earth.
Having trod upon the summit of the cosmic egg,
standing on the nail of his great toe.
Of single meaning, of the meaning of non-dual <s>dharma</s>,
the ultimate truth, the imperishable.
Of the meaning of various forms of consciousness,
the continuum of mind and consciousness.
Delighting in the meaning of all existences,
delighting in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), of foremost intellect.
Gone beyond attachment to existence and the rest,
the great delight of the three realms of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud,
with the beautiful radiance of autumn moonbeams.
With the hue of the disk of the rising sun,
with the radiance of the nails of great passion.
Clad in fine garments tipped with sapphire,
bearing great sapphire-blue hair-tips.
The glory of the rays of great jewels,
adorned with <s>Buddha</s>-emanations.
Shaking hundreds of world-realms,
of great strides through the bases of miraculous power.
The bearer of great <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), the truth itself,
the king of the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of the four foundations of mindfulness.
Fragrant with the blossoms of the factors of awakening,
the ocean of the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
The knower of the way of the <s>aṣṭāṅga-mārga</s> (eightfold path),
the knower of the path of the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>.
Greatly attached to all beings,
yet unattached, like the sky.
Born from the minds of all beings,
swift as the minds of all beings.
The knower of the faculties and purposes of all beings,
the course of the minds of all beings.
The knower of the truth of the meaning of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),
the holder of the purity of the five <s>skandhas</s>.
Abiding at the summit of all paths of liberation,
skilled in all paths of liberation.
Standing on the path of all liberations,
the teacher of all paths of liberation.
Having uprooted the twelve-limbed existence,
the holder of purity in twelve aspects.
Of the form of the method of the four truths,
the holder of the realization of the eight knowledges.
Of the truth-meaning in twelve aspects,
the knower of reality in sixteen aspects.
Awakened in twenty aspects,
fully awakened, the supreme knower of all.
The illuminator of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-emanation
body-multitudes.
Realizing all moments,
the knower of the meaning of all mind-moments.
Through various vehicles, methods, and means,
the illuminator of the welfare of the world.
Having emerged through the three vehicles,
established in the fruit of the one vehicle.
Whose self is purified of the realm of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the maker of the destruction of the realm of <s>karma</s>.
Having crossed over the ocean of the flood,
having emerged from the wilderness of <s>yoga</s> (bondage).
Having well abandoned <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), secondary afflictions, and defilements,
together with their latent impressions.
<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion)—
the infallible accomplisher of the welfare of the world.
Whose purpose has abandoned all perceptions,
whose purpose is consciousness, the holder of cessation.
The object of the minds of all beings,
the mental course of all beings.
Dwelling within the minds of all beings,
having attained equality with their minds.
The gladdener of the minds of all beings,
the delight of the minds of all beings.
The established doctrine, free from error,
devoid of all delusion.
Of doubtless mind, of triple purpose,
serving all purposes, of the nature of the three qualities.
Of the purpose of the five aggregates, of the three times,
the illuminator of all moments.
Awakened in a single instant,
the holder of the self-nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The formless body, the supreme body,
the illuminator of body-multitudes.
The displayer of all forms,
<s>Ratnaketu</s>, the great jewel.

body.translated_text: Twenty-four verses on the wisdom of equality.

children.translated_text: To be awakened by all perfectly awakened ones,
the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-awakening.
Syllable-less, the source of <s>mantras</s>,
the three families of the great <s>mantras</s>.
The generator of the meaning of all <s>mantras</s>,
the great <s>bindu</s> (point), syllable-less.
The five-syllabled one, the greatly empty,
empty of <s>bindu</s>, the hundred-syllabled one.
Of all forms, yet formless,
the holder of the half-of-half-of-sixteen <s>bindu</s>.
Without parts, beyond division,
the holder of the summit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
The knower of the parts of all meditations,
the knower of the families and lineages of <s>samādhi</s>.
The <s>samādhi</s>-body, the supreme body,
the king of all <s>saṃbhogakāyas</s> (enjoyment bodies).
The <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), the supreme body,
the holder of the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-emanations.
Creating universally in the ten directions,
accomplishing the welfare of the world as appropriate.
The god above gods, lord of gods,
<s>Surendra</s> (lord of gods), lord of <s>dānavas</s> (demons).
Lord of the immortals, <s>guru</s> of the gods,
the tormentor, lord of the <s>pramathas</s>.
Having crossed the wilderness of existence,
the sole teacher, <s>guru</s> of the world.
Renowned in the world of the ten directions,
the great lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>.
Clad in the armor of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),
shielded by the shield of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion).
With the sword, bow, and arrow of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the destroyer of the battle of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and ignorance.
The enemy of <s>Māra</s>, the conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the hero,
the ender of the fear of the four <s>Māras</s>.
The conqueror of all <s>Māra</s>'s armies,
the fully awakened one, the leader of the world.
To be venerated, to be worshipped, to be saluted,
to be honored perpetually.
Most worthy of worship, to be respected,
to be bowed to—the supreme <s>guru</s>.
Whose stride traverses the three worlds in a single step,
whose prowess extends to the limits of space.
Possessing the three knowledges, learned, purified,
possessing the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections).
<s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Mahāsattva</s> (great being),
transcending the world, of great supernatural power.
Grounded in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom),
having arrived at the reality of wisdom.
The knower of self, the knower of others, all-knowing,
belonging to all, indeed the foremost person.
Having surpassed all comparison,
the knowable one, the supreme lord of wisdom.
The best lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>,
the teacher of the meaning of the four <s>mudrās</s> (seals).
Most worthy of attendance among the worlds,
of those who traverse the three paths of liberation.
Of glory purified in the ultimate truth,
the great auspicious one of the three worlds.
The glorious one, the bestower of all prosperity,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the best among the glorious ones.

body.translated_text: Fifteen verses on the wisdom of accomplished action.

children.translated_text: Homage to you, O giver of boons, O foremost of <s>vajra</s>-holders,
O ultimate reality, homage to you.
Homage to you, O womb of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
O <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, homage to you.
O <s>Buddha</s>-passion, homage to you,
O <s>Buddha</s>-desire, repeated homage.
O <s>Buddha</s>-joy, homage to you,
O <s>Buddha</s>-delight, repeated homage.
O <s>Buddha</s>-smile, homage to you,
O <s>Buddha</s>-laughter, repeated homage.
O <s>Buddha</s>-speech, homage to you,
O <s>Buddha</s>-nature, repeated homage.
O one born from non-existence, homage to you,
homage to you, O one born from the <s>Buddha</s>.
O one born from space, homage to you,
homage to you, O one born from wisdom.
O net of illusion, homage to you,
homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s>-drama.
Homage to you—to all, to all,
O wisdom-body, homage to you.

body.translated_text: Thus end the five verses of praise to the wisdom of the five <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text:
iyam asau vajrapāṇe vajradhara bhagavato jñānamūrteḥ sarvatathāgatajñānakāyasya mañjuśrījñānasatvasyāveṇikapariśuddhā nāmasaṃgītiḥ | tavānuttaraprītiprasādamahaudbilyasaṃjananārthaṃ kāyavāṅmanoguhyapariśuddhyai | aparipūrṇāpariśuddhabhūmipāramitāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūripariśuddhyai | anadhigatānuttarārthasyādhigamāya | aprāptasya prāptyai | yāvat sarvatathāgatasaddharmanetrīsaṃdhāraṇārthaṃ ca mayā deśitā saṃprakāśitā ca vivṛttā vibhajitottānīkṛtā adhiṣṭhitā ceyaṃ mayā vajrapāṇe vajradhara tava saṃtāne sarvamantradharmatādhiṣṭhāneneti ||
punar aparaṃ vajrapāṇe vajradhara iyaṃ nāmasaṃgītiḥ suviśuddhaparyavadātasarvajñajñānakāyavāṅmanoguhyabhūtā | sarvatathāgatānāṃ buddhabodhiḥ | samyaksaṃbuddhānām abhismayaḥ | sarvatathāgatānām anuttaraḥ | dharmadhātugatiḥ sarvasugatānāṃ | sarvamārabalaparājayo jinānāṃ | daśabalabalitā sarvadaśabalānāṃ | sarvajñatā sarvajñasya jñānānāṃ | āgamaḥ sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ | samudāgamaḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ | vimalasupariśuddhapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūriḥ sarvamahābodhisatvānāṃ | prasūtiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ | kṣetraṃ sarvadevamanuṣyasaṃpatteḥ | pratiṣṭhā mahāyānasya | saṃbhavo bodhisatvacaryāyāḥ | niṣṭhā samyagāryamārgasya | nikaṣo vimuktīnāṃ | utpattir niryāṇamārgasya | anucchedas tathāgatavaṃśasya | pravṛddhir mahābodhisatvakulagotrasya | nigrahaḥ sarvaparapravādināṃ | vidhvaṃsanaṃ sarvatīrthikānāṃ | parājayaś caturmārabalacamūsenānāṃ | saṃgrahaḥ sarvasatvānāṃ | āryamārgaparipākaḥ sarvaniryāṇayāyināṃ | samādhiś caturbrahmavihāravihāriṇāṃ | dhyānam ekāgracittānāṃ | yogaḥ kāyavāṅmano 'bhiyuktānāṃ | visaṃyogaḥ sarvasaṃyojanānāṃ | prahāṇaṃ sarvakleśopakleśānāṃ | upaśamaḥ sarvāvaraṇānāṃ | vimuktiḥ sarvabandhanānāṃ | mokṣaḥ sarvopadhīnāṃ | śāntiḥ sarvacittopaplavānāṃ | ākaraḥ sarvasaṃpattīnāṃ | parihāṇiḥ sarvavipattīnāṃ | pithanaṃ sarvāpāyadvārāṇāṃ | satpatho vimuktipurasya | apravṛttiḥ saṃsāracakrasya | pravartanaṃ dharmacakrasya | ucchritacchatradhvajapatākās tathāgataśāsanasya | adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvadharmadeśanāyāḥ | kṣiprasiddhir mantramukhacaryācāriṇāṃ bodhisatvānām | bhāvanādhigamaḥ prajñāpāramitābhiyuktānāṃ | śūnyatāprativedhaḥ advayaprativedhabhāvanābhiyuktānāṃ | niṣpattiḥ sarvapāramitāsaṃbhārasya | pariśuddhiḥ
sarvabhūmipāramitāparipūryai | prativedhaḥ samyakcaturāryasatyānāṃ | sarvadharmaikacittaprativedhaś catuḥsmṛtyupasthānānāṃ | yāvat parisamāptiḥ sarvabuddhaguṇānām iyaṃ nāmasaṃgītiḥ ||
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, is the exclusively pure Chanting of the Names of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Wisdom-Being, who is the wisdom-body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the embodiment of wisdom of the Blessed One. For the purpose of generating in you unsurpassed joy, faith, and great elation; for the purification of the secrets of body, speech, and mind; for the fulfillment and purification of the incomplete and impure accumulations of merit and wisdom of the stages and perfections; for the attainment of the unattained supreme goal; for the obtaining of the unobtained; and for the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>-lamp of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>—it has been taught, proclaimed, revealed, analyzed, and made clear by me; and it has been empowered by me, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, in your continuum through the empowerment of the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>mantras</s>. Furthermore, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, this Chanting of the Names, being the thoroughly pure secret of body, speech, and mind of the omniscient wisdom-body, is: the <s>Buddha</s>-awakening of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; the realization of perfectly awakened ones; the unsurpassed of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; the course to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) of all <s>Sugatas</s>; the defeat of all <s>Māra</s>'s forces for the victorious ones; the strength of the ten powers for all who possess the ten powers; the omniscience of the omniscient one's wisdoms; the tradition of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; the complete attainment of all <s>Buddhas</s>; the fulfillment of the stainless and thoroughly pure accumulations of merit and wisdom for all great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the origin of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; the field of all divine and human prosperity; the foundation of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; the source of <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice; the culmination of the noble eightfold path; the touchstone of liberations; the origin of the path of liberation; the continuity of the <s>Tathāgata</s> lineage; the growth of the family and lineage of great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the subjugation of all rival doctrines; the destruction of all non-Buddhist teachers; the defeat of the armies of the four <s>Māras</s>; the gathering of all beings; the ripening on the noble path of all who traverse the paths of liberation; the <s>samādhi</s> of those who dwell in the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes); the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) of those with one-pointed minds; the <s>yoga</s> of those devoted to body, speech, and mind; the disjoining of all fetters; the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions; the pacification of all obstructions; the liberation from all bonds; the release from all substrates; the peace from all mental disturbances; the source of all prosperity; the decline of all misfortunes; the closing of all doors to evil destinies; the good path to the city of liberation; the cessation of the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>; the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>; the raised parasol, banner, and flag of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching; the empowerment of all <s>Dharma</s>-teachings; the swift accomplishment for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who practice the <s>mantra</s> approach; the meditative attainment of those devoted to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the penetration of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) for those devoted to the meditation of non-dual penetration; the accomplishment of the accumulation of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); the purification for the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s> of all stages; the penetration of the four noble truths; the penetration of all <s>dharmas</s> in one mind through the four foundations of mindfulness; and the completion of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities—this is the Chanting of the Names.
This is the benefit of the second cycle; its verses number fifty-two.

body.text:
punar aparaṃ vajrapāṇe vajradhara iyaṃ nāmasaṃgītiḥ sarvasatvānāṃ aśeṣakāyavāṅmanaḥsamudācārapāpapraśamanī | sarvasatvānāṃ sarvāpāyānāṃ viśodhanī | sarvadurgatinivāraṇī | sarvakarmāvaraṇānāṃ samucchedanī | sarvāṣṭākṣaṇasamutpādasyānutpādakarī | aṣṭamahābhayavyupaśamanakarī | sarvaduḥsvapnanirnāśanī | sarvadurnimittavyapohanakarī | sarvaduḥśakunavighnavyupaśamanakarī | sarvamārārikarmadūrīkaraṇī | sarvakuśalamūlapuṇyasyopacayakarī | sarvāyoniśomanaskārasyānutpādanakarī | sarvamadamānadarpāhaṃkāranirghātanakarī | sarvaduḥkhadaurmanasyānutpādanakarī | sarvatathāgatānāṃ hṛdayabhūtā | sarvabodhisatvānāṃ guhyabhūtā | sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ rahasyabhūtā | sarvamudrāmantrabhūtā | sarvadharmānabhilāpyavādināṃ smṛtisaṃprajanyasaṃjananī | anuttaraprajñāmedhākarī | ārogyabalaiśvaryasaṃpatkarī | śrīśubhaśāntikalyāṇapravardhanakarī | yaśaḥślokakīrtistutisaṃprakāśanakarī | sarvavyādhimahābhayapraśamanakarī | pūtatarā pūtatarāṇāṃ | pavitratarā pavitratarāṇāṃ | dhanyatamā dhanyatamānāṃ | māṅgalyatamā sarvamāṅgalyatamānāṃ | śaraṇaṃ śaraṇārthināṃ | layanaṃ layanārthināṃ | trāṇaṃ trāṇārthināṃ | parāyaṇam aparāyaṇānāṃ | dvīpabhūtā dvīpārthināṃ | agatikānām anuttaragatikabhūtā | yānapātrabhūtā bhavasamudrapāragāmināṃ | mahābhaiṣajyarājabhūtā sarvavyādhinirghātanāya | prajñābhūtā heyopādeyabhāvavibhāvanāyai | jñānālokabhūtā sarvatamondhakārakudṛṣṭyapanayanāya | cintāmaṇibhūtā sarvasatvayathāśayābhiprāyaparipūraṇāya | sarvajñajñānabhūtā mañjuśrījñānakāyapratilambhāya | pariśuddhajñānadarśanabhūtā pañcacakṣuḥpratilambhāya | ṣaṭpāramitāparipūribhūtā āmiṣābhayadharmadānotsarjanatayā | daśabhūmipratilambhabhūtā
puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasamādhiparipūraṇatayā | advayadharmatā dvayadharmavigatatvāt | tathatārūpatānanyadharmatādhyāropavigatatvāt | bhūtakoṭirūpatā pariśuddhatathāgatajñānakāyasvabhāvatayā | sarvākāramahāśūnyatārūpatā aśeṣakudṛṣṭigahanagatinirghātanatayā | sarvadharmānabhilāpyarūpeyaṃ nāmasaṃgītir yadutādvayadharmatārthaṃ nāmasaṃdhāraṇaprakāśanatayeti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, this <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names) pacifies all sins of body, speech, and mind of all beings without exception; purifies all evil destinies of all beings; prevents all misfortunes; completely destroys all karmic obscurations; prevents the arising of all eight unfavorable states; pacifies the eight great fears; annihilates all bad dreams; dispels all evil omens; pacifies all obstacles from evil portents; removes all actions of <s>Māra</s>-enemies; increases all merit from wholesome roots; prevents the arising of all improper mental attention; destroys all intoxication, pride, arrogance, and ego; prevents all suffering and mental distress; is the heart-essence of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; is the secret essence of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; is the mystery of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; is the essence of all <s>mudrās</s> and <s>mantras</s>; generates mindfulness and clear comprehension for all who teach the inexpressibility of all <s>dharmas</s>; produces supreme <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and intelligence; brings health, strength, sovereignty, and prosperity; increases glory, auspiciousness, peace, and well-being; reveals fame, praise, reputation, and eulogy; pacifies all diseases and great fears. It is the purest of the pure; the most sacred of the sacred; the most blessed of the blessed; the most auspicious of all the most auspicious. It is the refuge for those seeking refuge; the shelter for those seeking shelter; the protection for those seeking protection; the ultimate resort for those without resort; the island for those seeking an island; the supreme destination for those without destination; the vessel for those crossing the ocean of existence; the great king of medicines for destroying all diseases; <s>prajñā</s> for discerning what is to be abandoned and adopted; the light of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) for removing all darkness and wrong views; the wish-fulfilling gem for fulfilling the wishes and intentions of all beings; omniscient knowledge for attaining the <s>jñānakāya</s> (knowledge-body) of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; purified knowledge-vision for attaining the five eyes; the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> through generosity of material things, fearlessness, and <s>Dharma</s>; the attainment of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) through the completion of merit and knowledge accumulations and <s>samādhi</s>; non-dual <s>dharmatā</s> (reality) because it is free from the <s>dharma</s> of duality; the nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) because it is free from the superimposition of otherness; the nature of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (reality-limit) because of the nature of the purified <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>jñānakāya</s>; the nature of the great <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of all aspects because it completely destroys all wrong views and their deep entanglements. This <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> is inexpressible as all <s>dharmas</s>, that is, because it reveals names that hold the meaning of non-dual <s>dharmatā</s>.
This is the benefit of the third <s>cakra</s> (cycle); its verses number fifty-two.

body.text:
punar aparaṃ vajrapāṇe vajradhara yaḥ kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā mantramukhacaryācārī imāṃ bhagavato mañjuśrījñānasatvasya sarvatathāgatajñānakāyasya jñānamūrter advayaparamārthāṃ nāmasaṃgītiṃ nāmacūḍāmaṇiṃ sakalaparisamāptam anyūnām akhaṇḍām ebhir eva gāthāpadavyañjanaiḥ pratyaham akhaṇḍaṃ triṣkālaṃ dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati | parebhyaś ca vistareṇa yathāsamayaṃ yathāyogyato yāvat saṃprakāśayiṣyati pratyekaṃ cānyatamānyatamanāmārthaṃ | mañjuśrījñānakāyam ālambanīkṛtya ekāgramānaso bhāvayiṣyati | adhimuktitatvamanaskārābhyāṃ samantamukhavihāravihārī sarvadharmaprativedhikayā paramayā anāvilayā prajñānuviddhayā śraddhayā samanvāgataḥ saṃstasya tryadhvānadhvasamaṅginaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvāḥ samāgamya saṃgamya sarvadharmamukhāny upadarśayiṣyanti | ātmabhāvaṃ copadarśayiṣyati | durdāntadamakāś ca mahākrodharājāno mahāvajradharādayo jagatparitrāṇabhūtā nānānirmāṇarūpakāyair ojobalaṃ tejo 'pradhṛṣyatāṃ sarvamudrāmantrābhisamayamaṇḍalāny upadarśayiṣyanti | aśeṣāś ca mantravidyārājñyaḥ sarvavighnavināyakamārārimahāpratyaṅgirāmahāparājitāḥ sarātriṃdivaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ sarveryāpatheṣu rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyanti | sarvabuddhabodhisatvādhiṣṭhānaṃ kariṣyanti | sarvakāyavāṅmanobhis tasya saṃtāne samyag adhiṣṭhāsyanti | sarvabuddhabodhisatvānugraheṇa cānugrahīṣyanti | sarvadharmavaiśāradyapratibhānaṃ copasaṃhariṣyanti | sarvārhacchrāvakapratyekabuddhāryadharmapremāśayatayā ātmabhāvaṃ copadarśayiṣyanti | ye ca brahmendropendrarudranārāyaṇasanatkumāramaheśvarakārtikeyamahākālanandikeśvarayamavaruṇakuverahārītīdaśadiglokapālāś ca satatasamitaṃ sarātriṃdivaṃ gacchatas tiṣṭhataḥ śayānasya niṣaṇṇasya svapato
jāgrataḥ samāhitasyāsamāhitasya ca ekākino bahujanamadhyagatasya ca yāvad grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīmadhyagatasyendrakīlarathyāpratolīnagaradvāravīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakanagarāntarāpaṇapaṇyaśālāmadhyagatasya yāvac chūnyāgaragirikandaranadīvanagahanopagatasya ucchiṣṭasyānucchiṣṭasya mattasy pramattasya sarvadā sarvathā sarvaprakāraṃ ca parāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyanti | ratriṃdivaṃ paraṃ svastyayanaṃ kariṣyanti | ye cānye devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā manuṣyāmanuṣyāś ca ye cānye grahanakṣatramātṛgaṇapatayo yāś ca sapta mātaro yāś ca yakṣiṇīrākṣasīpiścācyas tāḥ sarvāḥ sahitāḥ samagrāḥ sasainyaḥ saparivārāḥ sarve te rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyanti | paraṃ ca tasya kāye ojobalaṃ prakṣepsyanti | ārogyabalam āyurvṛddhiṃś copasaṃhariṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family, practicing the <s>mantra</s>-approach conduct, should uphold, recite, master, and properly contemplate in mind this <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>—the <s>Nāmacūḍāmaṇi</s> (Crown Jewel of Names), the ultimate truth of the <s>jñānasattva</s> (knowledge-being) <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>jñānakāya</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the embodiment of <s>jñāna</s>, the non-dual ultimate reality—complete, unabridged, unbroken, with these very verse-syllables, daily, uninterruptedly, three times [a day]; and should extensively teach it to others at the proper time and in the proper manner, explaining each and every name and meaning; and should meditate single-mindedly, taking the <s>jñānakāya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> as the object of contemplation, dwelling in the all-encompassing abode through aspiration and true mental engagement, endowed with supreme, untainted faith penetrated by <s>prajñā</s>, penetrating all <s>dharmas</s>—for that one who possesses the three times as non-temporal, all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> shall come together, assemble, and reveal all <s>dharma</s>-doors; and shall reveal their own embodiment. And the tamers of the untamed, the great <s>Krodharājas</s> (wrathful kings) such as great <s>Vajradhara</s> and others, who serve as protectors of the world, through various emanation-form-bodies, shall reveal their vigor, power, splendor, invincibility, and all <s>mudrā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-<s>abhisamaya</s>-<s>maṇḍalas</s>. And all <s>mantra</s>-<s>vidyā</s>-queens, the great <s>Pratyaṅgirā</s> and great <s>Aparājitā</s> who [overcome] all obstacle-<s>Vināyakas</s> and <s>Māra</s>-enemies, shall provide protection, guarding, and shelter at all times, day and night, at every moment, in all postures. All <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> shall grant their empowerment; they shall properly empower that person's continuum with all body, speech, and mind; they shall grace [that person] with the grace of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; they shall bestow confidence and eloquence in all <s>dharmas</s>. And the <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, out of love for the noble <s>Dharma</s>, shall reveal their own embodiment. And <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Nandikeśvara</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kuvera</s>, <s>Hārītī</s>, and the ten direction-protectors shall constantly, day and night, whether one is walking, standing, lying down, sitting, sleeping, waking, concentrated or unconcentrated, alone or among many people, even when in villages, cities, market towns, districts, kingdoms, or capitals, at crossroads, streets, avenues, city gates, lanes, squares, intersections, or within markets and shops, or even when one has gone to empty houses, mountains, caves, rivers, forests, or thickets, whether ritually pure or impure, intoxicated or heedless—at all times, in all ways, in every manner, they shall provide supreme protection, guarding, and shelter. Day and night they shall ensure supreme well-being. And whatever other <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans and non-humans, and whatever lords of planets, constellations, and <s>mātṛ</s>-hosts, and the seven mothers, and whatever <s>yakṣiṇīs</s>, <s>rākṣasīs</s>, and <s>piśācīs</s>—all of them together, assembled, with their armies and retinues, shall all provide protection, guarding, and shelter. And they shall infuse supreme vigor and power into that person's body. They shall bestow health, strength, and increase of lifespan.
This is the benefit of the fourth <s>cakra</s>; its verses number nineteen.

body.text:
punar aparaṃ vajrapāṇe vajradhara ya imāṃ nāmasaṃgītiṃ nāmacūḍāmaṇiṃ pratyaham akhaṇḍasamādānatas triḥkṛtvā kaṇṭhagatām āvartayiṣyati | pustakagatāṃ vā paṭhamānaḥ pravartayiṣyati | bhagavato mañjuśrījñānasatvasya rūpam ālambayann anuvicintayaṃs tadrūpam anudhyāyan | tam eva rūpakāyenācirād eva dharmavinayam upādāya drakṣyati | gaganatalagatāṃś ca sarvabuddhabodhisatvān nānānirmāṇarūpakāyaiḥ sahagatān drakṣyati | na tasya mahāsatvasya jātu kadācit kathamapi durgatyapāyapatanaṃ ca bhaviṣyati | nīcakulopapattir na bhaviṣyati | pratyantajanapadopapattir na bhaviṣyati | na hīnendriyo bhaviṣyati | na vikalendriyo bhaviṣyati | na mithyādṛṣṭikulopapattir bhaviṣyati | nābuddheṣu buddhakṣetreṣūpapatsyate | na buddhotpādataddeśitadharmavimukhaparokṣatā bhaviṣyati | na ca dīrghāyuṣkeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate | na ca durbhikṣarogaśastrāntarakalpeṣūpapatsyate | na ca pañcakaṣāyakāleṣūpapatsyate | na ca rājaśatrucaurabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati | na ca sarvavaikalyadāridrabhayaṃ | na cāślokābhyākhyānanindāyaśo'kīrtibhayaṃ bhaviṣyati | sujātikulagotrasaṃpannaś ca bhaviṣyati | samantaprāsādikarūpavarṇasamanvāgato bhaviṣyati | priyo manaāpasukhasaṃvāsapriyadarśanaś ca lokānāṃ bhaviṣyati | śubhasaubhāgyādeyavākyaś ca satvānāṃ bhaviṣyati | sa yatra yatropapatsyate tatra tatra jātau jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati | mahābhogo mahāparivāro 'kṣayabhogo 'kṣayaparivāro bhaviṣyati | agraṇīḥ sarvasatvānām agraguṇasamanvāgato bhaviṣyati | prakṛtyā ca ṣaṭpāramitāguṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati | caturbrahmavihāravihārī ca bhaviṣyati | smṛtisaṃprajanyopāyabalapraṇidhijñānaiḥ samanvāgataś ca bhaviṣyati | sarvaśāstraviśārado vāgmī ca bhaviṣyati | spaṣṭavāgajaḍapaṭumatir bhaviṣyati | dakṣo 'nalasaḥ saṃtuṣṭo mahārtho vitṛṣṇaś ca bhaviṣyati | paramaviśvāsī ca sarvasatvānāṃ
bhaviṣyati | ācāryopādhyāyagurūṇāṃ ca saṃmato bhaviṣyati | aśrutapūrvāṇi ca tasya śilpakalābhijñājñānaśāstrāṇi cārthato granthataś ca pratibhāsam āgamiṣyati | supariśuddhaśīlājīvasamudācāracārī ca bhaviṣyati | supravrajitaḥ sūpasaṃpannaś ca bhaviṣyati | apramuṣitasarvajñatāmahābodhicittaś ca bhaviṣyati | na jātu śrāvakārhatpratyekabuddhaniyāmāvakrāntigataś ca bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, whoever shall recite this <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>, this <s>Nāmacūḍāmaṇi</s> (Crown Jewel of Names), three times daily with unbroken observance, memorized by heart, or reading from a manuscript, contemplating and reflecting upon the form of the Blessed <s>Mañjuśrījñānasattva</s>, meditating upon that form—that one shall soon behold the <s>Dharmavinaya</s> (Doctrine and Discipline) through that very form-body. And one shall behold all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the expanse of the sky, accompanied by various emanation-form-bodies. For that great being there shall never, at any time, in any way, be a fall into evil destinies or lower realms. There shall be no birth in a low family. There shall be no birth in a border region. One shall not have deficient faculties. One shall not have incomplete faculties. There shall be no birth in a family of wrong views. One shall not be born in <s>Buddha</s>-fields without <s>Buddhas</s>. There shall be no turning away from or indifference to the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s> taught by him. One shall not be born among long-lived gods. One shall not be born in <s>kalpas</s> (eons) of famine, disease, or weapons. One shall not be born in times of the five degenerations. There shall be no fear from kings, enemies, or thieves. There shall be no fear of any deprivation or poverty. There shall be no fear of disrepute, defamation, blame, ill-fame, or infamy. One shall be endowed with good birth, family, and lineage. One shall be endowed with an entirely pleasing form and complexion. One shall be dear, agreeable, pleasant to live with, and pleasing to behold for the world. One shall speak auspicious, fortunate, and welcome words to beings. Wherever one is born, in each and every birth, one shall remember past lives. One shall have great enjoyments and great retinue, inexhaustible enjoyments and inexhaustible retinue. One shall be the foremost of all beings, endowed with the foremost qualities. By nature, one shall be endowed with the qualities of the six <s>pāramitās</s>. One shall dwell in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes). One shall be endowed with mindfulness, clear comprehension, skillful means, power, aspiration, and knowledge. One shall be learned in all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) and eloquent. One shall have clear speech, keen and sharp intellect. One shall be skillful, diligent, content, purposeful, and free from craving. One shall be supremely trusted by all beings. One shall be esteemed by <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers), <s>upādhyāyas</s> (preceptors), and <s>gurus</s>. And arts, crafts, higher knowledges, wisdom, and <s>śāstras</s> never before heard shall spontaneously arise in their meaning and letter. One shall practice with thoroughly pure conduct, livelihood, and behavior. One shall be well-ordained and well-endowed. One shall never lose the great <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) of omniscience. And one shall never enter the fixed course of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.
This is the benefit of the fifth <s>cakra</s>; its verses number fifty-one.

body.text: evaṃ vajrapāṇe vajradhara aprameyaguṇasamanvāgato 'sau mantramukhacaryācārī bhaviṣyati | anyaiś cāprameyair evaṃprakārair evaṃjātīyair guṇagaṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati | acirād eva vajrapāṇe vajradhara paramārthanāmasaṃgītisaṃdhārakapuruṣapuṃgavaḥ susaṃbhṛtapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraḥ ksiprataraṃ buddhaguṇān samudānīyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate | analpakalyāṇaparinirvāṇadharmaḥ sarvasatvānām anuttaradharmadeśako 'dhiṣṭhito daśadiksaddharmadundubhir dharmarāja iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, that practitioner of the <s>mantra</s>-approach conduct shall be endowed with immeasurable qualities. And he shall be endowed with other immeasurable qualities of such kind and nature. Before long, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, that supreme person who upholds the ultimate <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>, having well-accumulated the stores of merit and knowledge, shall swiftly bring together the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> and shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Endowed with the <s>dharma</s> of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of no small goodness, he shall be the supreme teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings, empowered as the drum of the true <s>Dharma</s> in the ten directions—a <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of the Dharma).
This is the benefit of the sixth <s>cakra</s>; its verses are immeasurable.

body.text: oṃ sarvadharmābhāvasvabhāvaviśuddhavajra a ā aṃ aḥ | prakṛtipariśuddhāḥ sarvadharmā yaduta sarvatathāgatajñānakāyamañjuśrīpariśuddhitām upādāyeti a āḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ hara hara | oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ bhagavan jñānamūrtivāgīśvara mahāvāca sarvadharmagaganāmalasupariśuddhadharmadhātujñānagarbha āḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>! All <s>dharmas</s> are pure by nature of non-existence, <s>vajra</s>: <s>a ā aṃ aḥ</s>. All <s>dharmas</s> are primordially pure, that is, by taking up the purity of the <s>jñānakāya</s> (knowledge-body) of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>: <s>a āḥ</s>! The heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>: <s>hara hara</s>! <s>Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ</s>! O Blessed One, embodiment of <s>jñāna</s>, Lord of Speech, great Voice, <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-womb, stainless as the sky of all <s>dharmas</s>, supremely purified: <s>āḥ</s>!
Arrangement of <s>mantras</s>.

children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>,
delighted and satisfied, with hands joined in reverence,
having bowed to the Protector, the fully Awakened One,
the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
together with the other manifold Protectors,
the lords of secrets, the <s>Vajrapāṇis</s>,
along with the wrathful kings,
proclaimed aloud these words:
'We rejoice, O Protector!
Well spoken, well spoken!
A great purpose has been accomplished for us,
leading to the attainment of perfect awakening.
For the world, which is without a protector,
longing for the fruit of liberation,
this is the purified path to the highest good,
proclaimed according to the method of the <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion).
Profound, noble, and vast,
of great purpose, accomplishing the world's welfare,
for this is indeed the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
taught by the perfectly Awakened One.'

body.translated_text: These are the five concluding verses.

body.text: āryamāyājālāt ṣoḍaśasāhasrikān mahāyogatantrāntaḥpātisamādhijālapaṭalād bhagavattathāgataśākyamunibhāṣitā bhagavato mañjuśrījñānasatvasya paramārthā nāmasaṃgītiḥ parisamāptā ||
body.translated_text: From the <s>Ārya-Māyājāla</s>, from the chapter on the <s>Samādhijāla</s> (Net of Concentrations) contained within the sixteen-thousand[-verse] great <s>Yogatantra</s>, the ultimate <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names) of the Blessed <s>Mañjuśrījñānasattva</s>, spoken by the Blessed <s>Tathāgata Śākyamuni</s>, is completed.
